results.description: Personal data of EU persons must be stored in the EU or EEA.

questions.data_residency: Where is personal data stored in production?

results.why: Personal data of EU persons is hosted in Amazon RDS us-east-1 (United States). The accepted production regions are EU or EEA only.

actions: Migrate the production datastore that holds personal data to an EU or EEA region (for example eu-north-1 / Finland).
Stop processing EU personal data in this system until residency is compliant.
steps: Inventory which tables and object stores contain names, emails, or other personal data.
Choose an approved EU/EEA region and plan a cutover (snapshot, restore, DNS, secrets).
Update hosting documentation so the recorded residency is EU or EEA.
Re-run the compliance health check after production traffic is in the new region.

results.description: Production datastores holding personal data must use AES-256 at rest.

questions.encryption_at_rest: What encryption is used for production data at rest?

results.why: TLS terminates at the load balancer and disk encryption is not enabled on RDS. Transport encryption alone does not satisfy encryption at rest.

actions: Enable AES-256 (or an approved equivalent) encryption at rest on the production database and object stores.
Rotate any plaintext backups created while the volume was unencrypted.
steps: Turn on storage encryption for the production RDS instance (or recreate it from an encrypted snapshot).
Enable default encryption on the object-storage bucket used for exports.
Record encryption_at_rest as AES-256 in the project answers and re-validate.

results.description: A DPA must be signed when PII is processed; otherwise not_applicable.

questions.dpa_signed: Is a data processing agreement signed with every processor?

results.why: A data processing agreement is on file with the current processors, so this statement passes.

actions: No change required for this check.

results.description: Interactive production access must require MFA.

questions.mfa_for_production: Is MFA required for interactive production access?

results.why: Developers can open the cloud console and use a shared SSH key without a second factor. Password-only or shared-key production access is not allowed.

actions: Enforce MFA on the cloud console, SSH, and any jump hosts that reach production.
Retire the shared production SSH key in 1Password.
steps: Enable organisation-wide MFA (IdP / AWS IAM / Azure AD) and block console login without a second factor.
Replace the shared SSH key with per-person keys or SSO short-lived credentials.
Confirm mfa_for_production is yes, then re-run the health check.

results.description: Each processing activity must have a recorded lawful basis.

questions.lawful_basis: What is the lawful basis for processing personal data?

results.why: The project recorded legitimate interest for CRM analytics, which is an accepted lawful basis.

actions: No change required for this check.

results.description: Personal data must not be kept longer than the documented retention period.

questions.retention_policy: Is a finite retention period defined and enforced?

results.why: Event logs and CRM extracts are kept indefinitely. GDPR storage limitation requires a defined, enforced retention period.

actions: Publish a retention schedule (for example 24 months for analytics events, 12 months for marketing extracts).
Turn on automated deletion or anonymisation when the period expires.
steps: Agree retention periods with the DPO for each personal-data store.
Implement TTL, lifecycle rules, or a scheduled wipe job.
Document the schedule in the record of processing and set retention_policy to defined.
Re-run the health check.

results.description: A record of processing activities (RoPA) must exist for this project.

questions.ropa_recorded: Is this processing listed in the organisation RoPA?

results.why: Whether GrowthBoard is listed in the organisation’s record of processing activities was not answered, so this check cannot pass or fail yet.

actions: Confirm with the DPO whether GrowthBoard is already in the RoPA.
If it is missing, file the processing activity before the next health check.
steps: Email the Data Protection Officer with the product name, data categories, and processors.
Record ropa_recorded as yes once the entry exists, or leave it empty only while the DPO investigates.
Re-run the health check after the RoPA row is confirmed.

results.description: A DPIA is completed when analytics profiling of individuals is in scope.

questions.dpia_completed: Has a DPIA been completed (or marked not applicable)?

results.why: A data protection impact assessment is on file for CRM analytics profiling.

actions: No change required for this check.

results.description: Production subprocessors must be on the approved-vendor list.

questions.analytics_vendor: Is every production analytics/subprocessor on the approved list?

results.why: GrowthBoard pushes events to a third-party analytics vendor that is not on the approved-subprocessor list.

actions: Stop sending personal data to the unlisted vendor until procurement approves it.
Switch to an already-approved analytics tool, or start a vendor assessment.
steps: Name the current vendor and the personal data it receives.
Open a procurement ticket with Aalto IT Procurement (template: new subprocessor).
Either disable the integration or move to an approved vendor, then set analytics_vendor to approved.
Re-run the health check.
